issue.description: After the decoded-view review, inspect ADR-024 section 3.4, research/specs/secret-ruleset-v4.md section 3.4, the accepted secret-rejection-v1 contract, and bead redact behavior. Check how every derived-view match maps to valid raw half-open coordinates, including URI percent-decoding and envelope/span rules, and whether a consumer can revalidate the reported range before redaction. Use only clean-room specifications, public API documentation, and synthetic fixtures. Acceptance: record in this bead's notes a pass or actionable rejection with a concrete raw-range example from an independent fixture and the precise interoperability risk.
issue.notes:
BR-T35 raw-range follow-up, 2026-10-03 — ACTIONABLE REJECTION of current ruleset-v4 hash bad7c8102086d8128465e284b839673ceceb84b28e3ea7bf55835dfaee5ad5a9, scoped to §3.4 pending a normative mapping rule. Reviewed ADR-024 hash 508989f43c984b3a69ef529eaaf0d96ed1caa44873857e91b14aeaaa61de9c86; accepted secret-rejection-v1 hash f6aa7639a8ef1dd509b431853abf64db78d0923ef9e9d59b09e0a4e0e55df231.

Independent synthetic fixture A: UTF-8 field `é=` + `sk-or-v1-` + (`%61%31%62%32%63%33%64%34` repeated 8) + `!`. Under v4 §4.1 the normalized token body is the 64-hex-byte pattern `a1b2c3d4` repeated 8. In raw UTF-8 byte coordinates, the derived match is `[3,76)`, while its percent-encoded raw source envelope is `[3,204)` in a 205-byte field; both envelope endpoints are UTF-8 boundaries. The v1 fingerprint must cover raw bytes `[3,204)`, not normalized bytes. For ANSI removal, escape decoding, percent decoding, and dewrapping, define a source span for each output byte and set `start` to the first matched byte’s source start and `end` to the last matched byte’s source end, thereby including deleted bytes between them. In the decoded view every output byte maps to the whole encoded run. Require a nonempty range with `0 <= start < end <= field byte length` and valid UTF-8 slice boundaries.

URI ambiguity fixture B: password bytes are the 40-byte string `a1B2c3D4` repeated 5 followed by `%FF`, in a URI whose literal prefix is `postgres://u:` and whose literal suffix is `@db.test/x`. The raw password span is `[13,56)`. The alternating 40-byte value passes Q(v,8); leaving `%FF` literal under the printable-only normalized decoder yields 43 printable bytes that pass Q, while URI-specific percent-decoding to byte 0xFF fails Q predicate 1 (printable ASCII). Thus one interpretation reports a finding fingerprinted over `[13,56)` and the other reports none. §3.2 only decodes printable `%HH`, while §4.3 says URI credentials use percent-decoding; specify whether URI uses that view or a separate all-byte decoder.

Redact revalidation check: the current CLI accepts a fingerprint, not caller-supplied offsets. The live path resolves the fingerprint, then inside the redaction transaction rescans the current field and verifies fingerprint, rule, start/end, and that the range is a valid Rust string slice before replacement. This safely rejects a report produced with a different mapping, but does not make that report interoperable: the consumer cannot resolve it and redaction returns not-found/conflict; a consumer that instead trusts mismatched offsets risks replacing the wrong bytes or leaving encoded secret bytes behind. Require canonical mapping and URI semantics before claiming v4 findings are portable to bead redact.

Delivery/verification: review-only; no source or test files changed and no commit was made. `bead show beadrs-e78cea45` confirms revision 3 and reports “Checkpoint already current” (covered sequence 16672). `git status --short` contains pre-existing staged/unstaged checkpoint and unrelated source changes from other workers, so mandatory pre-close step 1 (all listed changes owned by this bead) cannot be met. I stopped before clean-archive definition-of-done and push and did not close the bead.
issue.title: Review raw-range reporting and bead redact revalidation for BR-T35

issue.description:
## Problem (verified 2026-08-29, bead 0.2.1)
`bead init --prefix demo` creates .beads/beads.db and config.json but no .beads/checkpoint/current.json; the checkpoint first appears after the first mutation (`bead create`). Consumers that verify the checkpoint pointer — NEEDLE's `needle doctor` prints `[FAIL] Checkpoint checkpoint/current.json not found` — see a broken workspace between init and the first bead, which is exactly the moment a new user runs their first health check.

## Deliverable
- `bead init` publishes an empty generation (current.json + forensic.jsonl + objects/) through the same publication path as a mutation, honouring `--no-auto-flush` and `checkpoint.auto_flush`.
- Re-running init on an existing workspace does not rewrite a non-empty checkpoint.
- `bead doctor` on a fresh init reports the checkpoint as valid.
- Tests: fresh init -> current.json exists and points at a zero-issue generation; init with --no-auto-flush -> absent; re-init on a populated store -> checkpoint unchanged.

## Definition of done
Tests green; `bead init && bead doctor` in a temp dir is clean; a git-tracked fresh workspace commit contains the initial checkpoint.
issue.title: bead init publishes an initial checkpoint (current.json) so a fresh workspace has no dangling pointer until the first mutation
